summary: This survey distills a series of workshops on data-locality abstractions into a layered view of libraries, languages, runtimes and system-scale tools. Its distributed-memory content is qualitative: it classifies libraries by scale and languages by local-versus-global object visibility, and it calls for common abstractions across these layers.
why_read: It gives a newcomer shared terminology for layout, decomposition and placement, and a map of how locality abstractions for distributed-memory systems fit across the software stack.
main_contribution: A common terminology and a layered survey of data-locality abstractions, closing with recommendations for interoperable abstractions and runtime interfaces.
main_limitation: The authors state that they do not claim to have solved or covered every aspect of the challenge, and their library comparison is a deliberately simple sketch.
